Definition: Stable identifier for the canonical record.
Concise observable problem without assuming root cause.
Example: Dispense fails after aspiration because destination lid remains assigned.

Quality check: At least one; primary code identified.
Why it exists: Connects records to the evidence atlas.

Definition: Vendor, model, modules, interface, software, firmware.
Why it exists: Prevents applying advice outside its tested environment.

Definition: Labware, liquid, geometry, workflow, scientific constraints.
Error text, trace, measurement, screenshot, or reproduction.
Quality check: Evidence must be linked to the same run/configuration.
Confirmed requires reproduction or decisive evidence.

Definition: Validated procedure, correction, workaround, or disposition.
Quality check: Must state what changed and what was tested.
Example: Corrected tip length and position; merged PRs

Allowed values / format: Logic; interface; simulation; dry; wet; assay; production
0 unspecified; 1 declared; 2 measured; 3 device-validated; 4 independently reproduced
Why it exists: Makes resource and procedure credibility visible.

Definition: State of samples, resources, run, and scientific result.
Example: Material returned to source; tips discarded

Definition: Documentation, code, PR, test, dataset, or guide.
Why it exists: Canonical knowledge should point to maintained artifacts.

Definition: Conditions under which the answer may fail.
Quality check: At least one limitation or 'none known'.
Example: Not validated for all tip lots

Quality check: Must be updated after material changes.

Definition: Person, team, or project responsible for review.
Quality check: Must be reachable through public channel.

Definition: Original discussion and relevant post range.
Why it exists: Returns visibility and credit to the forum.

Allowed values / format: Active; review due; disputed; superseded; archived
